newsitem.title: USA: US Diagnostic says deal was not accretive.
newsitem.headline: US Diagnostic says deal was not accretive.

text.p: US Diagnostic Inc on Monday said negotiations to acquire American Shared Hospital Services had ended because a merger would not have been accretive.
"At this time, we do not have any plans on further discussions with American Shared," said Joseph Scime, US Diagnostic's director of investor relations.
Earlier Monday American Shared said merger talks had ended with US Diagnostic, which provides radiology services, mainly at diagnostic imaging centers.

The companies had agreed to a cash deal in December. The next month they revised their pact to a stock deal in which U.S. Diagnostic was to issue $2.40 of stock for each outstanding share of American Shared.

Soon thereafter, US Diagnostic disclosed it was under investigation by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, which led to changes in senior management and a significant decline in its stock price, American Shared said.
Shares of US Diagnostic were trading as high as 13-3/8 in January, Scime said. On Monday afternoon the shares were trading at 6-5/8, up 21/64.
Scime also said the company was still not interested in an April 3 offer from Medical Resources Inc, which had proposed buying US Diagnostics for $6.25 a share.
"We're not interested at all. The stock is very undervalued," Scime said.
